bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 3, 2026 2:07 PM Bihar: Water level in Ganga river rises increasing flood threat in new areas Bihar has been witnessing a continuous rise in the water level of the Ganga in Patna and several other districts. This has increased the threat of floods in new areas. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Disaster Management Department has issued an alert in view of the rising water level of the Ganga. According to the department, the river is likely to cross the Highest Flood Level at Gandhi Ghat in Patna tonight and at Hathidah in Mokama tomorrow afternoon. People living along the river and in low-lying areas of Bhojpur, Patna, Saran, Vaishali, Nalanda, Begusarai, Lakhisarai and Jehanabad have been advised to remain alert and avoid taking any risks. They have also been advised to stay away from rivers, ghats and waterlogged areas and follow the instructions of the local administration. In case of an emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at 1070.

bihar_raw_news.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP over youth protests | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 03, 2026 Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP against suppressing voice of youth Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday backed students and youngsters in Bihar who protested against alleged irregularities in the examination system, and warned the BJP that any government that suppresses the voice of the youth will eventually have to answer to the people. Gandhi made the remarks after meeting students and young people who, he said, had faced “horrific police brutality” while raising their concerns over the examination system. “Police lathis as well as gunfire from AK-47 and pistols left many students injured. A young man aspiring to serve the country in the Army had his leg battered by an AK-47 bullet -- and with it, his life-long dream was also shattered,” Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. He said the protesters were only demanding fair opportunities, a transparent examination system and their rights. “What was the need to use lathis and bullets in response to such demands?” Gandhi asked. He also rejected any attempt to hold only lower-ranking officials responsible for the police action. “The government cannot absolve itself of responsibility for such extreme brutality by merely blaming a few low-ranking officials. This action is either the result of orders from above or a sign of the administration's utter failure,” he said. Gandhi said he stood with the protesting youngsters and was ready to provide them with all possible assistance. “The BJP should remember: any regime that suppresses the voice of the youth eventually has to answer to the people. That day is not far off,” he said. Patna witnessed clashes between job aspirants and police last month after protesters tried to march towards the chief minister’s residence, demanding a single-tier teacher recruitment examination and a transparent recruitment process. The students’ agitation, which began in the first week of August, has received support from opposition leaders, including RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

Authorities have initiated the dismissal process. BPSC TRE Row: Non-Domicile Candidates Recruited on Low CTET Scores Facing Termination Key Points Major discrepancies found in BPSC TRE 2.0 & 3.0 background checks for non-domicile teachers. Non-domicile candidates secured posts with CTET scores below 90, claiming Bihar-only relaxations. Termination proceedings initiated; teachers appointed in 2021 face dismissal & salary recovery. A huge discrepancy has been found during the background document verification of the candidates who were selected under the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE) 2.0 and 3.0 phases. Official audits linking BPSC candidates' documents with the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET) scorecards revealed that several non-domicile applicants secured the primary and middle school teaching positions despite failing to meet the mandatory qualification requirement for unreserved candidates. Education department officials in districts like Muzaffarpur have initiated termination proceedings against the candidates from neighbouring states who wrongfully claimed local reservation relaxations. Domicile Vs. Non-Domicile Score Requirements As Per CTET Rules Under the recruitment rules set by the Bihar Education Department, candidates residing outside Bihar are classified strictly under the Unreserved (General) category, regardless of their native state’s reservation status or disability quotas. To qualify for the BPSC TRE appointment, candidates' scorecards must meet the requirements set, which are as follows:- Bihar Domicile Candidates:- Eligible candidates for state-level relaxed score criteria ( e.g., 55% or 82 marks for OBC/BC, and 50% or 75 marks for SC/ST/Divyang candidates). Non-Domicile Candidates (Outside Bihar):- Candidates must secure a minimum of 60% marks (90 out of 150) in the CTET exam to qualify for the unreserved general seats. During the folder audits in the primary schools (Classes 1 to 5), the authorities found out-of-state candidates appointed with CTET scores as low as 81 or 82 marks after incorrectly claiming disability (Divyang) relaxations intended solely for Bihar residents. bihar_raw_news.title: HUDCO rises after signing Rs 25000 crore MoU with Bihar government
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / Markets / Capital Market News / HUDCO rises after signing Rs 25,000 crore MoU with Bihar government HUDCO rises after signing Rs 25,000 crore MoU with Bihar government Last Updated : Sep 03 2026 | 12:16 PM IST Housing & Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) rose 2.06% to Rs 182.02 after signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Government of Bihar. Under the MoU, HUDCO will provide financial assistance of up to Rs 25,000 crore over five years for industrial infrastructure development in Bihar. The MoU was signed on 2 September 2026 in Patna. The funds will be provided as term loans for industrial infrastructure development, including land acquisition for proposed industrial parks. The Government of Bihar has entrusted the Infrastructure Development Authority (IDA) with facilitating and implementing industrial park and other infrastructure projects across the state. The loans will be provided in tranches through the statutory authority designated by the state government. HUDCO will offer flexible terms, including a moratorium and repayment period of up to 25 years. The loans will also have an option for prepayment. Repayment will be made from project-generated revenue or other ring-fenced sources, including identified receivables or the state budget. Separate operational agreements will be signed for individual projects, covering their scope and terms. bihar_raw_news.title: Health services under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana normal, says ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 02 Sep, 2026 Health services under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana normal, says Haryana govt Business To Business, Chandigarh, 02 September 2026: The Haryana government said on Wednesday that health services under the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) continued normally in the state. It added that despite the Indian Medical Association's (IMA) call to suspend services under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries in the state did not face any major difficulty in availing treatment. The state government said the State Health Agency continuously monitored the situation. Regular coordination was maintained with district-level officials, District Implementation Managers and empanelled hospitals. All empanelled hospitals were directed to continue treatment and health services as usual, while giving priority to eligible patients under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Hospitals were also instructed to ensure that no eligible beneficiary faced any unnecessary difficulty in availing treatment under the scheme. According to the State Health Agency, no complaint has been received regarding any eligible patient being denied treatment or any disruption in health services under the Ayushman Bharat scheme since the night of August 31 when it was stopped. The responses received from hospitals, along with the number of claims submitted during this period, also make it clear that beneficiaries continued to receive health services under the scheme. The State Health Agency has termed reports published in some newspapers regarding outstanding dues of Rs 12,000 crore to hospitals under the Ayushman Bharat scheme as factually incorrect. It said that such information creates unnecessary confusion among beneficiaries and the public. The actual status of payments and claims under the scheme is examined as per the prescribed procedure. The authority has appealed to the public not to rely on unverified reports or incomplete information and to trust only accurate and official information. The State Health Agency has also made it clear that if any beneficiary complains that an empanelled hospital refused to provide treatment under the Ayushman Bharat scheme on August 31 or September 1, the matter will be investigated as per the prescribed procedure. It will review complaints and information received from hospitals. If the investigation establishes that any hospital refused treatment to an eligible beneficiary under the scheme or deliberately obstructed treatment, appropriate action will be taken against the hospital concerned in accordance with the rules. The State Health Agency has assured all eligible families covered under the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana that they can continue to avail treatment at empanelled hospitals across the state as per the prescribed procedure. Beneficiaries have been urged not to be influenced by rumours, unverified information or misleading reports. bihar_raw_news.title: Jan Suraaj to contest 8 MLC seats in Bihar , Prashant Kishor says candidate names soon
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 02 Sep, 2026 Jan Suraaj to contest 8 MLC seats in Bihar, Prashant Kishor says candidate names soon Business To Business, Patna, 02 September 2026: Political activity surrounding the upcoming Bihar Legislative Council elections has intensified, with Jan Suraaj announcing plans to field candidates for eight seats. Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor made the announcement following an organisational meeting held in Muzaffarpur on Wednesday. The meeting, held at a hotel in the Zila Parishad Market area, was attended by office-bearers and workers from Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Sheohar and Vaishali. Discussions focused on the organisation's current strength, voter outreach and preparations for the upcoming elections in the Tirhut Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies. Party workers were invited to provide feedback on potential candidates and the organisation's preparedness for the elections. Leaders interested in contesting the polls also put forward their claims and shared their views on the electoral process. Prashant Kishor listened to the suggestions and discussed the selection of potential candidates with party functionaries. Speaking to the media after the meeting, he said the primary purpose of the gathering was to seek feedback on candidate selection and understand the political situation at the local level. He said leaders holding key organisational positions had been invited because of their knowledge of local conditions and voter sentiment. Kishor added that Jan Suraaj is preparing to contest eight MLC seats, while simultaneously working to strengthen its organisational structure and expand its reach among voters. He also urged party workers to actively participate in the election campaign and strengthen the organisation at the grassroots level. On questions about Jan Suraaj's support base, Kishor said the organisation's actual strength would ultimately be determined by the election results. He said workers and supporters were keen for the party to contest the MLC elections with full force and that there was considerable enthusiasm within the organisation. Kishor further said party workers wanted to build on the momentum generated by Jan Suraaj's victory in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll. The organisation has therefore stepped up preparations for the MLC elections, with a focus on activating its booth- and regional-level network and increasing direct outreach to voters. The Muzaffarpur meeting also covered election strategy, organisational strengthening and voter mobilisation. With deliberations on potential candidates underway, Jan Suraaj is expected to announce its candidates in the coming days. The announcement of the candidates is likely to provide greater clarity on the electoral contest in the Tirhut region and could further intensify political activity ahead of the Legislative Council polls. bihar_raw_news.title: India's record wheat harvest opens $1.5 bn export window amid policy shifts
bihar_raw_news.content: Business 02 Sep, 2026 India’s record wheat harvest opens $1.5 bn export window amid policy shifts Business To Business, New Delhi, 02 September 2026: India’s record wheat harvest, comfortable stocks, and recent liberalisation of export rules are expected to unlock over $1.5 billion in export opportunities, a report said on Wednesday. The report from industry chamber ASSOCHAM said the government has shifted specified wheat varieties, wheat flour and related products from “Prohibited” to “Free.” The shift will expand market access for Indian producers and processors while supporting export earnings in products such as wheat, durum wheat, atta, maida, semolina/rava and related items. It would support export earnings, expand global market opportunities for Indian producers and processors, and strengthen India’s role in the international wheat trade. The report said India has strong demand prospects in Egypt, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Algeria and the Philippines, aided by competitive pricing, geographic proximity and comfortable supply position. India's geographical location offers shorter shipping distances and lower freight costs to major importing countries in South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. These advantages improve the overall competitiveness of Indian wheat compared with supplies from many other exporting nations. The global wheat market is changing due to weather disruptions, geopolitical tensions, higher freight costs and fluctuations in production and prices. The Russia-Ukraine conflict has affected the traditional supply routes while extreme weather is creating uncertainty for major producers. These developments are also pushing large wheat-importing countries to look for more diversified and reliable sources. The USDA has projected that global wheat production will decline from a record 844 MMT in 2025-26 to around 819 MMT in 2026-27 while demand is expected to remain strong. The USDA said the primary contributors to this decline in wheat production will be major exporting nations including the United States, the European Union, Argentina and Australia. India produced a record 121 MMT of wheat in 2025-26 against domestic consumption of around 111 MMT. The wheat stock in the Central Pool stood at 51.3 MMT against the prescribed buffer norm of 27.5 MMT for 1 July as on May 28, 2026. The report also mentioned India’s strong price advantage, with wheat MSP around $268 per tonne compared with an international wheat price of about $303 per tonne in May 2026. bihar_raw_news.title: Animal and Fisheries Resources Dept, Bihar advises people not to consume fish caught ...
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 1, 2026 10:34 AM Animal and Fisheries Resources Dept, Bihar advises people not to consume fish caught from floodwaters Amid the floods in Nepal and the rising water levels of rivers in Bihar, the Animal and Fisheries Resources Department has advised people not to consume fish caught from floodwaters. According to the department, during floods, fish may come into contact with sewage, dead animals and other contaminated substances, increasing the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. Consumption of such fish may be harmful to health. The department has clarified that fish caught from floodwaters should not be used for consumption until the floodwater has stabilised and the condition of water bodies has returned to normal. The department has also appealed to people not to consume fish that appear unknown or unusual. People have been advised to avoid buying, selling or consuming fish caught from floodwaters.

bihar_raw_news.title: Flood situation worsens across Bihar as major rivers rise | Akashvani News - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 2, 2026 9:53 PM Flood situation worsens across Bihar as major rivers rise Patna: Waterlogged bank of the swollen Ganga River during the monsoon season in Patna, Bihar, on Wednesday, September 02, 2026. (Photo: IANS) The flood situation in Bihar continues to remain grim. After the Ganga, Gandak and Kosi rivers, the rising water level of the Son River has now affected several areas of North, Central and South Bihar. Our correspondent reports that Floodwaters from the Ganga have spread into low-lying areas of several districts, including Bhagalpur, Khagaria, Samastipur, Patna, Buxar, Bhojpur and Vaishali. Bhagalpur remains the worst-affected district. Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary said that although the flood situation in the district is dangerous, it remains under control. Meanwhile, the water level of the Son River has risen following the release of water from the Bansagar Dam in Rohtas. With the river in spate, all 69 gates of the Indrapuri Barrage have been opened. There is a possibility of water spreading into adjoining riverine and low-lying areas. In Aurangabad district, rising water levels in the Son, Batane, Punpun, Dhawa, Adari, Madar and Keshhar rivers have affected several villages. In Jehanabad district, the Dardha River is in spate, with floodwaters flowing over three bridges and culverts at Jafarganj, Shakurabad and Sai Mandir. Riverine areas in Buxar, Khagaria, Samastipur and Vaishali districts are also affected by floods. Relief and rescue operations are underway in the affected areas.

bihar_raw_news.content: The development of industrial parks requires significant upfront investment in land and supporting infrastructure. Access to long-term financing can help state authorities undertake such projects in a more structured and time-bound manner, particularly as Bihar looks to develop industrial infrastructure across different districts. Advertisment Shares of Housing & Urban Development Corporation Limited have risen 1.85% to Rs. 181.67 against the previous closing price of Rs.178.35. The stock opened at Rs. 181.82 and traded in the range of Rs. 184.69 to Rs. 180.50 during the day. The company's market cap is Rs. 36,364.51 crore. Project Development and Funding Structure HUDCO and the Bihar Government signed a MOU on September 2, 2026. HUDCO will provide up to Rs. 25,000 crore for various industrial infrastructure projects and land acquisition. The Bihar State has given the responsibility of implementing these projects to the Infrastructure Development Authority (IDA). IDA will have the power to acquire, buy, and develop land for these industrial parks. The respective authority selected by the government will be responsible for drawing the loan as needed. HUDCO will give the loan on very easy terms and conditions with a moratorium and repayment period of 25 years. Advertisment Repayment Structure The agreement provides that repayment of the loans will be supported through escrow of revenue generated from the projects or by ring-fencing other sources of revenue, including identified receivables or the state budget. This mechanism is intended to ensure timely repayment to HUDCO. The MoU also states that separate operational agreements will be executed between the parties, with the specific scope of work and terms and conditions to be mutually agreed upon based on the requirements of individual projects. Importantly, the MoU represents the intent of both parties to undertake the stated activities and does not itself constitute a disbursement of the entire Rs. 25,000 crore. The agreement will remain valid for three years from the date of execution, subject to annual review. Advertisment What Comes Next The next key development will be the identification and execution of individual industrial park projects and the corresponding operational agreements. The actual utilisation of the proposed financing will depend on project requirements and the tranches availed by the designated state authority. The company has not disclosed details of individual projects, loan disbursement schedules or the expected financial contribution from the arrangement at this stage. Therefore, the direct impact on HUDCO’s revenue and profitability cannot yet be determined. About the company Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited (HUDCO) is a premier techno-financing public sector enterprise focused on housing and urban infrastructure development in India. Established in 1970, it provides financial assistance for housing and infrastructure projects through government agencies, urban local bodies and other institutions. Its portfolio spans social housing, residential projects and community infrastructure, along with urban infrastructure sectors such as roads, energy, water and sewerage, industrial infrastructure, airports and seaports. bihar_raw_news.title: Maharashtra land bank to accelerate infrastructure development: CM Fadnavis
bihar_raw_news.content: National 02 Sep, 2026 Maharashtra land bank to accelerate infrastructure development: CM Fadnavis Business To Business, Mumbai, 02 September 2026: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Wednesday that the Maharashtra Land Bank digital system will accelerate the development of infrastructure projects across the state and ensure the guaranteed availability of land for compensatory afforestation. The Maharashtra Land Bank digital system -- a unified dashboard -- has been developed to consolidate information on land owned by various state government departments onto a single platform. The system was officially launched following Tuesday's Cabinet meeting. Additional Chief Secretary (Revenue) Vikas Kharge, Additional Chief Secretary (Forest) Milind Mhaiskar, and Settlement Commissioner Shailesh Naval presented a detailed briefing on the dashboard, the government statement said. By bringing all government land data under one digital umbrella, the Maharashtra Land Bank aims to streamline land searching, verification, and allocation processes. "The system supports optimal land utilisation, rapid department-specific land mapping, reduced decision-making delays, and enhanced administrative transparency. Furthermore, it enables comprehensive performance reviews via department-, district-, taluka-, and village-wise data aggregation and progress tracking," the Chief Minister said. "As an integrated digital framework for data-driven management of public land, the initiative synthesises land records, physical site inspections, GIS analysis, and MIS reporting to render state land governance efficient, transparent, and swift. Previously, fragmented land records across multiple administrative levels created hurdles in accessing timely information regarding land availability, current status, area, usage, and conditions of allocation violations. The Maharashtra Land Bank integrated digital system was specifically engineered to resolve these bottlenecks by offering a single, updated repository," the statement added. Key operational features of the Land Bank System include record verification, on site inspection and validation, integrated data repository, taluka. level access, GIS based analytics and digital land requisition process. According to the government statement, the Land Bank System will be useful to conduct initial checks of survey numbers, total area, and land classifications based on e-Pherphat (electronic mutation records) and existing documentation, field inspections to verify physical ground reality, remaining unallocated area, and instances of condition violations and aggregation of fragmented data sources into a secure digital central repository. There will be also be a dedicated portal logins for Tehsildars to update allocation statuses and log condition breaches for government lands and Occupant Class-II (Bhogwatdar Varg-2) lands. "The location-aware mapping will be instrumental to conduct spatial analysis of available land parcels and pending allocation matters. End-to-end online workflows for government departments will be helpful to submit requisitions, register applications, and undergo scrutiny, verification, and approval. The portal also features real-time site inspection logging complete with GPS coordinates, timestamps, and date stamps," the statement said. Addressing the roundtable organised by the Consulate General of India in association with Bank of America, Ms Sitharaman said India continues to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy despite global disruptions and challenges, the Finance Ministry said on X today. Moreover, she highlighted a range of reforms, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, saying these measures have provided greater regulatory certainty, eased compliance and reduced paperwork under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Finance Minister also said the government has focused on creating capital assets and supporting industry through infrastructure development, particularly in aviation, while also fostering a conducive investment climate, the ministry said. Other focus areas include promoting artificial intelligence and data centres, supporting global capability centres, ensuring credit availability to micro, small and medium enterprises and reducing non-performing assets of banks, she said. Ms Sitharaman also reiterated India’s commitment to fiscal prudence and discipline despite continuing challenges facing the global economy since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 165 PM Narendra Modi calls for greater adoption of water-saving technologies & learning from glo...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for sensitising Urban Local Bodies to the challenges arising from urbanisation, including population growth and future water requirements, and suggested organising similar Chintan Shivirs for Urban Local Bodies. Mr Modi chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Water, organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti yesterday. He called for greater adoption of water-saving technologies. He also suggested dedicated exhibitions and workshops, including exposure to global best practices, to enable Indian manufacturers and stakeholders to develop and scale efficient solutions. Prime Minister appreciated the intensive two-day deliberations and emphasised that the actionable and time-bound action points emerging from the Summit should be pursued through a continuous process of review and learning. He suggested that the Summit should not remain a one-time exercise and called for a continuous process of review and follow-up. Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Mr Modi suggested promoting “Jal Utsav” to create greater awareness among people. Prime Minister called for making de-silting a regular programme and developing clear criteria and SOPs for de-silting. On dam safety, he stressed rigorous preparedness before every monsoon, adherence to prescribed precautions and creating awareness among school students, including through suitable incorporation in educational curricula. PM Modi further called for strengthening knowledge and capacity on water management and governance in universities and higher educational institutions. He suggested structured interstate study visits involving public representatives, officials and farmers to facilitate practical learning and replication of successful interventions. Prime Minister called for robust water data governance, with water-sector data brought together, systematically managed, analysed and effectively utilised. He recommended the use of AI for data collection and analysis through a uniform format. He also stressed anticipatory and integrated planning to address water scarcity through suitable utilisation of treated water for agriculture and industrial purposes.

national_raw_news.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly adopts resolution urging Centre to recognise Tamil as HC’s principal language 26 mins ago 24
national_raw_news.content: Tamil Nadu Assembly today unanimously adopted a resolution urging the Union Government to take immediate and necessary action to facilitate the use of Tamil as the principal language of the Madras High Court. Moving the resolution at the State Assembly, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay pointed out that under Section 2 of the Tamil Nādu Official Language Act 1956, Tamil has been declared as the official language, and under Sections 4-A and 4-B of the Act, legal recognition has been provided for recording evidence in Tamil in the civil and criminal courts, tribunals, tent courts and revenue Courts functioning under the High Court. The Chief Minister also noted that under Article 348(2) of the Constitution of India, a constitutional mechanism is provided whereby the Governor of a State, with the previous consent of the President of India, may authorise the use of the official language of the State in the proceedings of the High Court. The resolution passed in the Assembly underlines the need to reconsider the necessity of making Tamil the principal language and establish appropriate procedures for petitions, documents and arguments filed or presented in Tamil, as significant advancements have been made in legal Tamil, translation, e -courts, technology-enabled translation and legal databases. The Statement also mentioned that Artificial intelligence technologies have advanced to the extent that speech in Tamil can be simultaneously rendered and heard in English. The resolution also suggested training in legal Tamil and translation for Judges, advocates and Court Personnel and take all necessary legal measures on proposals to be forwarded by the Governor of the State under Article 348 (2) of the Indian Constitution and Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963. Speaking on the resolution, members from various parties supported the Government and said that this is a definitive move so that a common man can understand his case related arguments happening to him or her.

national_raw_news.title: Two-day Drass Festival to begin tomorrow in Ladakh 2 hours ago 50
national_raw_news.content: In Ladakh, the upcoming two-day Drass Festival, scheduled for September 4 and 5, will provide a major platform to showcase the tourism, cultural and adventure potential of Drass, recently announced as a new district. Speaking to Akashvani, Deputy Commissioner Drass, Imtiyaz Kacho, said the revival of the Drass Festival has assumed special significance following the recent formation of the new district. He said the Drass Festival was organised in the past but had witnessed a gap in recent years. The District Administration has now taken the initiative to revive the festival, even on a modest scale this year, to generate renewed interest and highlight the identity and potential of the newly announced district. DC Imtiyaz Kacho said there is tremendous enthusiasm among the people, with interest and queries pouring in from across Ladakh and outside the Union Territory. He said the District Administration aims to develop Drass as an important tourist destination on the national map by promoting its spectacular natural landscapes, rich culture, heritage, adventure tourism and traditional sports. The Drass Festival will feature a wide range of activities, including eco-adventure and nature tours, visits to heritage sites, Horse Polo, Tent Pegging, cultural programmes and youth activities. The festival will also focus strongly on youth engagement, providing school and college students platforms to showcase their hidden talents through cultural, sporting and other extracurricular activities. Being organised under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, the festival will include awareness programmes, theatre performances and cultural events highlighting the dangers of drug and substance abuse. Programmes promoting patriotism and national unity will also form an important part of the celebrations. The second day of the festival coincides with Teachers’ Day, and special programmes will be organised to honour teachers. The celebrations will conclude with a cultural evening at the iconic Mannan Top View Point at Lamochan. Various institutions and departments, including Power Grid Corporation, the Army, BRO and other government departments, are supporting the initiative.
